short_lead_route_sector_test.warning: The unit is a GOES detection proxy in a fixed 20 km sampled sector; the model did not pass validation and January alerts cluster around one ongoing regional incident.

firms_independent_satellite_crosscheck.product: NASA FIRMS VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21 Standard Processing.
firms_independent_satellite_crosscheck.warning: The alert-selected FIRMS cohort is positive-only; its 20 km coincidences are regional and repeated rows refer to an ongoing event. No detection is not a verified no-fire label.

independent_near_route_event_check.source: Independent January SNMF event audit against frozen GOES model outputs.
independent_near_route_event_check.interpretation: SNMF reports a controlled incident near the route during the held-out January test; the frozen GOES model had valid pixel coverage but did not alert. The daily incident report does not establish ignition hour or GOES observational completeness.

full_trail_10km_frozen_GOES_sensitivity.warning: No GOES positives occurred in the 10 km validation or test labels, so precision cannot be estimated; a nearby official SNMF incident had valid pixels but no model alert.

gfs_24h_snmf_daily_report_proxy_episode_.warning: Consecutive route-day alert streaks against an incomplete SNMF report proxy are not physical fire precision or independent fire-event counts.

snmf_daily_negative_label_audit.interpretation: No report in the acquired January archive was an empty national event report. This cohort cannot supply explicit nationwide no-fire days; no nearby event in a daily PDF remains a report-based proxy, not a verified physical negative.
limitations: 1 of 31 dates had no PDF at the checked public archive paths; these dates are unobserved, not negative.
A missing report is not a fire-free observation and is not encoded as a negative label.
A repeated event is deduplicated by province/name/start date and rounded coordinates; records without coordinates use province/name/start date only.
Automated extraction requires spot-checking against the original PDF; no row without parsed coordinates is used in spatial matching.

snmf_2022_route_cohort_readiness.interpretation: The archived 2022 extraction has no records with numeric latitude/longitude, so it cannot extend a route-specific event cohort. This is missing spatial information in the extraction, not evidence of no incidents or fire-free days. The original PDFs or a geocoded incident registry are needed to recover spatial labels.
limitations: 2 of 274 dates had no PDF at the checked public archive paths; these dates are unobserved, not negative.

external_label_audit.monthly_year_coverage_verified_by_audit: 1999-2025; 27 annual and 27 monthly GeoTIFF objects listed in the public bucket; the 2025 raster checksum was verified.
limitations: Monthly retrospective scar pixels do not establish ignition time or future prediction accuracy.

The product page text still summarizes monthly maps as 2013-2024, while MapBiomas's September 2026 collection launch states monthly and annual products for 1999-2025; the public-bucket inventory and verified 2025 raster support the extended coverage.

minimum_independent_alert_evidence_examp.method: One-sided 95% exact Clopper-Pearson lower bound. Alerts must be adjudicated against independent labels and be independent episodes; repeated pixels, scans, and adjacent days do not count separately.
minimum_independent_alert_evidence_examp.warning: These are precision-only sample-size examples. They do not provide power for recall, calibrate a probability, validate lead time, or account for event clustering beyond the unit definition.

persistence.report_cohort: SNMF explicitly said no fires were reported nationally; not a physical-fire negative survey.
persistence.interpretation: A VIIRS class 7-9 pixel is independent thermal-detection corroboration, not proof of wildfire or model correctness. No VIIRS detection is not proof of absence.

frozen_modis_model_independent_viirs_cro.interpretation: No VIIRS class 7-9 detections corroborated the logistic/XGBoost alerts in this small test. Two route buffers had no class-5 land sample; even class-5 samples are partial, so these are not verified physical-fire negatives and do not estimate model precision.

limitations: SNMF explicit no-fire reports describe the administrative record and do not prove physical absence.
VIIRS classes 7-9 are independent thermal detections, not adjudicated wildfire truth.
A daily 1 km composite can miss small, obscured, or between-overpass fires; class 5 is partial observation only.
NASA CMR returned no VNP14A1.002 granule for one requested date/tile; that alert is unknown and excluded from observed counts.
The cohort contains only frozen model alerts on selected report dates; it cannot estimate precision, recall, calibration, or forecast reliability.
The 0.1 score threshold is diagnostic and the model scores are not calibrated probabilities.

viirs_observations_on_all_route_days_wit.interpretation: This is an observation-coverage and sensor-coincidence audit on selected administrative no-fire report dates. Missing detections are not verified physical negatives, and the selected cohort does not estimate predictive precision or recall.

limitations: The administrative SNMF no-fire wording does not prove that no physical fire existed.
VIIRS classes 7-9 are thermal detections, not adjudicated wildfire truth.
NOAA-20/21 class 5 with QA land is partial observed clear land, not complete sensor coverage of a route buffer.
Daily 1 km composites can miss small, obscured, or between-overpass fires.
The three VIIRS platforms share an instrument family and algorithm lineage; their detections do not replace independent field-confirmed labels.
This selected set of report dates cannot estimate model precision, recall, calibration, or forecast skill.
The 0.1 model score cutoff is diagnostic and is not a calibrated probability.

existing_375m_same_day_event_coordinate_.interpretation: Exact-date I-band overpasses at the reported point do not establish whether a fire was active before or after the pass. Cloud/quality, no matching pass, and clear-land without detection are separate observation states, not fire/no-fire ground truth.

daily_l3_download_and_independent_positi.warning: This is a selected positive-event corroboration fraction, not model precision, recall against all physical fires, or a rate of false negatives. Route-date observations are not guaranteed independent physical incidents.

daily_viirs_l3_label_candidate.interpretation: The daily L3 positive-event pilot is downloaded and decoded. It corroborates only 2 of 15 selected SNMF route-dates with a same-day VIIRS fire pixel within 10 km; report-point cells are clear-land samples, and the cohort has no verified negatives. This is independent event-coincidence evidence, not model precision or a physical-fire false-negative rate.

fire_mask_classes.rule: Only class 5 may serve as an observed no-detection label; classes 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6 are not negative samples. Apply Algorithm QA and land/route checks before use.

geolocation_pilot.interpretation: One exact-time mask/geolocation pair yielded quality-valid class-5 clear-land observations near the route. This validates a path to observed non-detection labels for individual overpasses, not physical no-fire labels or model precision.

geolocation_companion_cohort_readiness.interpretation: All exact-time companions were downloaded and hash-verified; their actual local size is reported above. The evidence still covers only one seven-day corridor case.

full_route_observation_screen.interpretation: Across 61 same-week sensor passes, 60 contained quality-valid class-5 clear-land pixels within the 10 km route buffer, and none contained a quality-screened classes 7, 8 or 9 detection there. These repeated observations from one corridor and short event window are not 61 independent fire/no-fire cases; SNMF lacks an exact ignition time. This improves observation coverage labels but cannot estimate model precision.

goes_alerts_same_time_viirs_observation_.interpretation: Only VIIRS passes acquired during a GOES alert interval are listed. Class 5 is a clear-land non-detection at that pass; it does not establish an alert as false because this is one corridor and the incident labels lack exact ignition time.

full_swath_viirs_observation_candidate.interpretation: All 61 full-swath fire-mask granules and their 61 exact-time geolocation companions were downloaded and hash-verified (9.143 GB actual companion size). Across the 10 km route buffer, 60 passes had quality-valid class-5 clear-land pixels; none had a quality-screened classes 7, 8 or 9 detection, and one pass had no eligible clear-land pixel. These repeated observations from one corridor do not establish event truth or estimate model precision.

historical_viirs_snmf_event_route_screen.interpretation: The 2025 archive has clear-land observations at some reported incident coordinates, but dates are report start dates, not exact ignition or sensor times. No fire-class pixel was found on sampled route vertices in this screened cohort; it is a coverage and label feasibility check, not a prediction evaluation.

noaa_efire_barda_case_study.interpretation: Two full-geolocation NOAA E-FIRE passes observed quality-valid clear land at the Barda coordinate; one pass had all 103 sampled trail vertices clear, the next had 44 clear and 59 bowtie. This is a useful pixel-level non-detection case, but one reported event and two passes without exact ignition time cannot validate model precision or establish physical absence.

noaa_efire_route_overpasses_2024_07_10.interpretation: The 18:31 UTC overpass had cloud-class pixels at all 127 sampled Condorito vertices, so the nearby JMA alert remains unverified by this pass. Che Roga had 117 clear-land samples with no fire class 7-9. Frey and Bosque Tallado had only cloud or bowtie samples. These are single-pass pixel observations, not independent fire/no-fire route-days and do not change model precision evidence.

nasa_firms_nrt_prospective_crosscheck.interpretation: All 24 archived NOAA/NASA FIRMS NRT queries for the two date range returned valid empty CSVs, with no records within 10 km of the eight full route polylines. NRT is a provisional positive-only source; this empty snapshot is not a no-fire observation or a precision estimate. The period should be refreshed from standard processing after NASA's product lag.

nasa_firms_standard_availability_for_pro.interpretation: At query time on 2026-10-23, NASA FIRMS VIIRS standard products were available only through 2026-06-30, 115 days before the target end date; no standard detections could be queried for the prospective window. This is missing product availability, not evidence of no fire.

inpe_prospective_window_status.interpretation: The refreshed daily INPE file has no listed detections within 10 km of the complete route polylines in the available partial intervals. The Oct 23 CSV remains immature and active-fire rows are not a sensor-coverage mask. Three forecast windows are waiting for an immature CSV and five for missing CSVs; no complete 24-hour outcome or precision estimate is available.

route_geometry_for_prospective_join.detection_spatial_rule: within 10 km of the complete reviewed route polylines, using a local planar point-to-segment distance
route_geometry_for_prospective_join.forecast_index_spatial_rule: INPE risk values remain sampled at route-sector centers.
route_geometry_for_prospective_join.interpretation: The observation join now uses complete reviewed trail polylines; the forecast raster sampling is still center-based.

viirs_clear_land_completeness_on_2024_ex.interpretation: High clear-land fraction supports a well-observed VIIRS non-detection for the sensor-detection target, not proof of physical fire absence. This selected negative-report cohort has no detected fire positives, is clustered in time, and cannot estimate fire-alert precision, recall, or prevalence. JMA alerts without VIIRS detections are disagreement cases, not confirmed false alarms.

global_fire_atlas_daily_ignition_route_c.interpretation: GFA adds daily positive event candidates derived from burned-area progression. Its dates are inferred at daily resolution, it has no verified negative route-days, and it cannot validate hourly lead time or alert precision. INPE coincidences are positive-source corroboration and may share satellite platforms; SNMF corroborates only the small selected event subset.

idecor_ohmc_fwi_prospective_capture.interpretation: The official Córdoba map supplied one current-day and one next-day FWI layer at five route points. This starts prospective collection; it is one route-date, the points are spatially dependent, the map response has no WRF initialization timestamp, and FWI is fire-behaviour danger rather than calibrated ignition probability.

data_needed_to_resume_a_defensible_test: A complete timestamped incident/active-fire registry for the eight Argentina route corridors, with coordinates or perimeters, source observation time, confidence/quality, and explicit sensor-coverage gaps. The newer GFA screen adds 20 positive event-route records (16 with nearby INPE detections and 2 matched to the available SNMF event subset), but its inferred day-level starts do not provide observed ignition times or verified negatives.

More independently adjudicated no-fire windows for those corridors. The 2024 VIIRS cohort now provides 122 route-days with at least 90% clear-land coverage across 14 report-date clusters for the sensor-detection target, but its 27 dates were selected from SNMF no-fire reports and do not establish physical fire absence.

The daily 1-km VNP14A1/VJ114A1/VJ214A1 pilot now covers all 216 route-days on 27 selected 2024 dates; 122 have at least 90% clear-land coverage and 79 are fully clear by the sampled-grid criterion. This supports evaluation of the satellite-detection target, but the cohort has no positive fire detections and cannot establish physical no-fire labels. Extend it with independently timed positive events and broader prospective dates while retaining clouds, unprocessed classes, missing tiles and incomplete observations as unknown.

Historical or prospectively archived weather forecasts with issue time and valid time, paired to independent fire observations. The first official OHMC/IDECOR FWI snapshot is only one route-date and does not expose the WRF initialization timestamp; continue daily captures and adjudicate event and observed no-fire outcomes.
At least the required number of independent, adjudicated alert episodes for a chosen precision bound, plus a later untouched season for final evaluation.

next_external_candidate.dataset: NASA FIRMS standard-science active-fire archive (VIIRS S-NPP/NOAA-20/NOAA-21 and MODIS)
next_external_candidate.why_useful: An independent active-fire sensor family could corroborate GOES alerts and add historical event detections.
next_external_candidate.access: A NASA FIRMS MAP_KEY and NASA_EARTHDATA_TOKEN are configured in the ignored local .env. The 61 exact-time NASA VNP03IMG/VJ103IMG/VJ203IMG granules were downloaded, hash-verified, and paired with VNP14IMG/VJ114IMG/VJ214IMG masks for the Barda corridor.
data_limits: FIRMS is an active-fire detection archive, not a complete fire/no-fire panel.
NASA notes that fires can be missed between satellite overpasses or under cloud, heavy smoke, or tree canopy; such absences cannot be labeled negative without valid observation/quality coverage.
NRT data are replaced by standard detections after roughly 2-5 months; NASA recommends standard science-quality data for research.
next_external_candidate.required_companion_data: A per-pixel or per-route observation/quality mask for each overpass, plus independently archived forecast issue/valid times and official incident/perimeter records. A complete route-time cohort still requires valid fire-free periods or another independent source that can verify non-events.
